claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- OpenAI scraps rollout of new model over safety concerns: The firm also issued an update on incidents in which its models accessed Australian government systems.
- Evicted Spanish pensioner can move back home, lawyer says: The eviction of Maricarmen Abascal, 87, prompted large-scale protests across Spain.
- Argentina threatens legal action against UK over Falkland Islands oil exploration: President Javier Milei set a two-week deadline for the Sea Lion oilfield project to be scrapped.
- New York Times executive fatally shot allegedly by elderly in-laws: Jonathan McKinsey's in-laws, who are both 77 years old, face multiple charges including first-degree murder.
- US ban on Canadian alcohol and dairy comes into effect as trade war drags on: It is the latest escalation in the Canada-US trade war after negotiations collapsed in late August, with no word on when talks may resume.
- French PM warns against escalation of school protests after 164 arrested: Students are protesting over issues such as overcrowded classes, but the prime minister has condemned reports of violence.
- Tennessee governor declines to halt execution of state's lone woman on death row: If the execution proceeds, Pike would be the first woman put to death in Tennessee in more than 200 years.
- Lost songs from iconic Australian rockstar found in garage: Divinyls frontwoman Chrissy Amphlett recorded the songs with Split Enz's Tim Finn in 1998.
- Seoul summons Ukraine envoy over North Korean prisoner-of-war row: Last week Zelensky revealed Ukraine had sent two captured North Koreans to South Korea - which Seoul says was meant to be a secret.
- Twelve women have been killed in one part of South Africa since July. Here's what we know so far: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa says the murders are a "stain on our national conscience".
- Nigerian attempts to break world record by dancing non-stop for seven days: Crowds have gathered in Lagos to watch Ben Dancer, who says he will carry on dancing until Tuesday morning.
- Iran court upholds lashes sentence for singer who performed without hijab: Parastoo Ahmadi was convicted of "offending public decency" after singing while wearing a sleeveless dress during a livestreamed concert.

image_provider.prompt: A fractured mirror or broken glass surface with jagged, angular shards in various states of reflection and darkness, some fragments catching dim light while others fall into shadow. The composition suggests things coming apart—boundaries dissolving, trust shattering. Dark tones dominate with occasional glints of reflected color. Render in a style evoking both fragmentation and loss of clarity, as if viewing multiple conflicting realities simultaneously through broken planes.
